ai.title: Hemolytic Anemia
ai.subject: Medicine
ai.summary: Hemolytic anemia is the premature destruction of red cells, leading to anemia, jaundice and hemoglobinuria. In low‑resource settings, malaria, sickle cell, infections and herbal toxins are common causes.

sections.p: Hemolytic anemia results when red blood cells (RBCs) are destroyed faster than they are produced. The body responds with increased erythropoiesis, but the net effect is a fall in hemoglobin and red cell indices.

t.b: Shows spherocytes, schistocytes or bite cells – indicates extravascular or intravascular hemolysis

sections.p: The key to managing hemolytic anemia is to identify the underlying mechanism: immune, hereditary, enzymatic, mechanical, infectious or toxic.

sections.p: Patients present with fatigue, pallor, jaundice, dark urine, splenomegaly and sometimes acute chest or renal failure. Early recognition prevents irreversible organ damage.
